title: Drywall Software: 10 Tools for Drywall Contractors
html:
Drywall software works best as a short stack: a job app, an estimate app and a free search presence. Most drywall contractors need a scheduling and invoicing tool, a photo tool and a Google Business Profile before anything else. Start with drywall marketing basics and a search engine optimization plan that covers your site. Published plans below run from free to $299 a month.

Drywall software has to do three jobs: run the crew, price the job and bring in the next lead. Many drywall shops buy one big app and never open half of it. This guide groups ten tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Drywall work moves in phases: hang, tape, mud, sand and finish. Each phase has a crew, a drying window and a punch list, so scheduling slips fast. A drywall contractor also competes on search for remodels, repairs and new builds.

What does each drywall software tool do and cost?

The table lists all ten tools by job, with the entry price each vendor shows. Use it to shortlist, then read the details below.

ToolJob it doesEntry price shown by the vendorMain limit
JobberScheduling and invoices$49 a month, no commitmentExtra users cost $29 a month
Housecall ProScheduling and invoices$59 a month billed annuallyAdd-ons have no listed price
JoistEstimates and invoices$10 a month billed monthly5 documents a month on Basics
Contractor ForemanProject management$49 a month billed annuallyNo monthly billing on Basic
CompanyCamJob photos$63 a month billed annually2-user limit on Core
Search ConsoleSearch dataFreeYour own site only
Ahrefs Webmaster ToolsAudit and backlinksFree5,000 crawl credits a month
SemrushKeywords and rank tracking$139 a month, or $117.33 billed annually500 keywords tracked daily
BrightLocalLocal rank tracking$41 a month billed monthly100 keywords per location
Google Business ProfileMap listingFreeNeeds verification and upkeep

Entry prices read from each vendor page in November 2026. Check the vendor for current plans.

Which drywall software runs jobs and crews?

Jobber and Housecall Pro are the two job apps that drywall contractors compare first. Both handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments in one place.

  • Jobber: covers scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. The Core plan for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: each extra user costs $29 a month, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are billed on top.
  • Housecall Pro: covers scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments. Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Essentials is $149 a month billed annually for five users. Limit: the page lists several add-ons without prices, so confirm the full cost before you sign.

Both vendors charge card processing fees on top of the plan. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents for credit cards and 1% for bank payments. Housecall Pro says its card rates start at 2.59%. A drywall crew that invoices large remodel jobs feels those fees, so ask each vendor for your rate in writing.

Pick the app by crew size. One lead installer with a helper can start on a single-user plan. A shop that runs two or three finishing crews at once needs a plan with more seats. Add seats only when you have the schedule to fill them.

Which drywall contractor software handles estimates and invoices?

Joist is an estimate and invoice app, which makes it a light choice for a small drywall crew that does not need dispatch.

  • Joist: sends estimates and invoices and takes online payments. Basics is $10 a month billed monthly, and Pro is $17 a month billed monthly. Limit: Basics allows up to 5 documents a month, so a busy crew outgrows it quickly.

Drywall quotes depend on square footage, ceiling height, board thickness, finish level and any hauling of old material. Build one template per job type: new hang and finish, patch and repair, and basement finishing. A template lets you send a quote the same day as the walk-through.

Quote speed also feeds search. Homeowners compare several quotes, and the first clear one usually wins. A matching website design with a short quote form shortens that gap further.

Which drywall software tracks projects and job photos?

Contractor Foreman and CompanyCam cover the project side. One tracks budgets and documents, and the other keeps dated photos tied to each job.

  • Contractor Foreman: project management with pricing per company instead of per user. Basic is $49 a month billed annually for one user, and Standard is $105 a month billed annually for up to 3 users. Limit: Basic is not sold on monthly billing, and Basic and Standard do not include pricing in the Local Material Database.
  • CompanyCam: job photo capture with project folders. Core is $63 a month billed annually and includes one user, with a 2-user limit. Limit: extra users cost $29 each, and Core caps video at 5 minutes.

Photos protect a drywall shop. A dated photo of a finished joint or a pre-existing crack settles most callback disputes. Those same photos also make good proof for your site and your Google profile.

Which drywall SEO tools find homeowners searching for you?

Google Search Console, Ahrefs Webmaster Tools, Semrush and BrightLocal each answer a different SEO question. Start with the two free ones and add paid tools only when you can act on the data.

  • Google Search Console: shows the queries and pages that bring impressions and clicks, and flags indexing problems. Google describes it as a free service. Limit: it needs a Google account and site verification, and it reports your own site only.
  • Ahrefs Webmaster Tools: a free site audit and backlink view for sites you verify. Ahrefs lists unlimited verified websites. Limit: Site Audit gets 5,000 crawl credits per project each month, and Site Explorer shows up to 1,000 backlinks and 1,000 keywords at a time.
  • Semrush: keyword research and daily rank tracking. The SEO plan lists $139 a month, or $117.33 a month billed annually, with 500 keywords tracked daily. Limit: the page shows custom pricing for its Advanced tier, and a small drywall shop will not use most of the plan.
  • BrightLocal: local rank tracking, citation checks and review tools. Track is $41 a month billed monthly for one location, or $31 a month billed annually. Limit: Track follows up to 100 keywords per location, and building new citations costs extra, starting at $3.20 per site.

A drywall site should rank for jobs near the shop, such as repair, finishing and remodel drywall in your service towns. Use Search Console to see which towns already bring impressions.

Which free tool puts a drywall contractor on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows a drywall company in Google Maps. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, hours, photos, reviews and phone number when homeowners search nearby. Limit: your address must meet Google's guidelines and you must verify the business, and a listing without fresh photos and review replies rarely stands out.

What numbers should drywall software track?

Drywall software should track five numbers: calls, quotes sent, quotes won, days from walk-through to quote, and revenue per job. Without them, you cannot tell whether a tool pays for itself.

  • Quote speed: measure the days between the walk-through and the sent quote. Aim to cut it before you buy anything else.
  • Win rate: divide won quotes by sent quotes each month. A drop after a price change tells you where to look.
  • Revenue per job: compare repair jobs with full finishing jobs. Most shops find the two behave like different businesses.
  • Lead source: note whether each call came from search, the map listing, ads or a referral. Put a dollar value on each source so you can see which one pays.

Most job apps record the first three numbers, and they only record the last two if you enter them. That one field makes the tool far more useful for marketing decisions.

How should a drywall shop set up its first 30 days of software?

Set up one tool a week, in order of how directly it protects revenue. Do not roll out everything at once, because a crew only adopts one new habit at a time.

  • Week 1: claim the Business Profile, verify Search Console and load your service towns. Both are free.
  • Week 2: choose an estimate app, build three quote templates and send the next real quote from it.
  • Week 3: add job photos at the start and end of every job, and name each folder by address.
  • Week 4: review the numbers above, then decide whether a full job app earns its monthly price.

Keep one person in charge of each tool. When nobody owns the photo app, the photos stop within a month. When nobody owns the estimate templates, quotes go back to scribbled numbers.

How do you choose drywall software?

Choose drywall software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it quote by square foot or by line item, and can you attach photos and a finish level to the quote?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users and card processing fees, then compare the total with one average repair job and one average finishing job.

Setup effort: can one person load templates and customers in a weekend, or does it need training and an onboarding fee?

Shop sizeStarter stackPublished price from the vendors above
Solo finisherJoist Basics, Business Profile, Search Console$10 a month billed monthly, plus free tools
Two-person crewJobber Core, CompanyCam Core, Business Profile$49 a month with no commitment, plus $63 a month billed annually
Multi-crew shopHousecall Pro Essentials, Contractor Foreman Standard, BrightLocal Track$149 and $105 a month billed annually, plus $41 a month billed monthly

Example stacks built from the plan prices above, read from each vendor in November 2026. Taxes, extra users and card fees are not included.

A solo finisher can run on a $10 estimate app and the free Google tools. A multi-crew shop fits a full job app better.

What software does a drywall contractor need?

A drywall contractor needs a way to quote jobs, schedule crews and collect payment. It also needs a website and a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find the shop. Start with an estimate and invoice app, then add job management once you run several crews at once.

How much does drywall software cost?

Plans here run from free, for Business Profile and Search Console, to $299 a month for the top Housecall Pro plan. That price is billed annually. Joist Basics costs $10 a month billed monthly. Card fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so check each vendor before you buy.

Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a drywall contractor?

Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually. Run the free trial each vendor offers before you commit.

What is the best drywall estimating software?

No single tool wins every shop, so use a stated test: quote speed, photo attachments and total monthly cost. Joist is the lightest paid option here at $10 a month billed monthly, and Jobber adds scheduling. Test two apps on one real quote before you choose.

Do drywall companies need a website if they use job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A site with a page for each town and job type, plus a quote form, gives homeowners a reason to call you first.

Are there free drywall SEO tools?

Yes. Google Search Console is a free Google service, and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools is free for sites you verify. Google Business Profile also costs nothing to add or claim. Paid tools like Semrush and BrightLocal add rank tracking, but you can start with the free three.

What should a new drywall company buy first?

Claim a free Google Business Profile and set up Search Console first. Then add an estimate and invoice app such as Joist. Move to full job management only when scheduling several crews becomes the bottleneck, because extra seats and add-ons raise the monthly price quickly.

shows your name, service area, hours, photos, reviews and phone number when homeowners search nearby. Limit: your address must meet Google's guidelines and you must verify the business, and a listing without fresh photos and review replies rarely stands out.
##
What numbers should drywall software track?
Drywall software should track five numbers: calls, quotes sent, quotes won, days from walk-through to quote, and revenue per job. Without them, you cannot tell whether a tool pays for itself.
-
Quote speed:
measure the days between the walk-through and the sent quote. Aim to cut it before you buy anything else.
-
Win rate:
divide won quotes by sent quotes each month. A drop after a price change tells you where to look.
-
Revenue per job:
compare repair jobs with full finishing jobs. Most shops find the two behave like different businesses.
-
Lead source:
note whether each call came from search, the map listing, ads or a referral. Put a dollar value on each source so you can see which one pays.
Most job apps record the first three numbers, and they only record the last two if you enter them. That one field makes the tool far more useful for marketing decisions.
##
How should a drywall shop set up its first 30 days of software?
Set up one tool a week, in order of how directly it protects revenue. Do not roll out everything at once, because a crew only adopts one new habit at a time.
-
Week 1:
claim the Business Profile, verify Search Console and load your service towns. Both are free.
-
Week 2:
choose an estimate app, build three quote templates and send the next real quote from it.
-
Week 3:
add job photos at the start and end of every job, and name each folder by address.
-
Week 4:
review the numbers above, then decide whether a full job app earns its monthly price.
Keep one person in charge of each tool. When nobody owns the photo app, the photos stop within a month. When nobody owns the estimate templates, quotes go back to scribbled numbers.
##
How do you choose drywall software?
Choose drywall software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
does it quote by square foot or by line item, and can you attach photos and a finish level to the quote?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra users and card processing fees, then compare the total with one average repair job and one average finishing job.
Setup effort:
can one person load templates and customers in a weekend, or does it need training and an onboarding fee?

###
What software does a drywall contractor need?
A drywall contractor needs a way to quote jobs, schedule crews and collect payment. It also needs a website and a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find the shop. Start with an estimate and invoice app, then add job management once you run several crews at once.
###
How much does drywall software cost?
Plans here run from free, for Business Profile and Search Console, to $299 a month for the top Housecall Pro plan. That price is billed annually. Joist Basics costs $10 a month billed monthly. Card fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so check each vendor before you buy.
###
Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a drywall contractor?
Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually. Run the free trial each vendor offers before you commit.
###
What is the best drywall estimating software?
No single tool wins every shop, so use a stated test: quote speed, photo attachments and total monthly cost. Joist is the lightest paid option here at $10 a month billed monthly, and Jobber adds scheduling. Test two apps on one real quote before you choose.
###
Do drywall companies need a website if they use job software?
Yes. Job software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A site with a page for each town and job type, plus a quote form, gives homeowners a reason to call you first.
###
Are there free drywall SEO tools?
Yes. Google Search Console is a free Google service, and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools is free for sites you verify. Google Business Profile also costs nothing to add or claim. Paid tools like Semrush and BrightLocal add rank tracking, but you can start with the free three.
###
What should a new drywall company buy first?
Claim a free Google Business Profile and set up Search Console first. Then add an estimate and invoice app such as Joist. Move to full job management only when scheduling several crews becomes the bottleneck, because extra seats and add-ons raise the monthly price quickly.
